children: A group of Iranian lawmakers has called on President Masoud Pezeshkian to nominate a new intelligence minister. The request, made in a letter, emphasizes the need for a candidate who meets legal qualifications and lacks partisan affiliations. This appeal comes amid ongoing discussions in Iran's parliament about potentially altering the requirements for the intelligence minister role, which currently include clerical qualifications that some lawmakers wish to remove. The position has remained vacant since the previous minister, Esmail Khatib, was killed earlier this year.
Lawmakers' request to President Pezeshkian suggests continued debate over the qualifications for Iran's intelligence minister.
The absence of a permanent intelligence minister since March indicates ongoing instability in Iran's political landscape.
Market pricing suggests a potential increase in the likelihood of President Pezeshkian's departure, reflecting concerns over political stability.

Observers will be monitoring the Iranian parliament's actions regarding the statutory requirements for the intelligence minister. Any changes in these requirements could shift the current political dynamics. Additionally, any public statements or actions from key figures like Ayatollah Ali Khamenei or the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps could influence market perceptions of President Pezeshkian's political future. The market currently implies a 6.5% probability that Pezeshkian will no longer be president by the end of the year.

title: Iranian lawmakers urge President Pezeshkian to nominate new intelligence minister
